newsitem.title: VIRGIN ISLANDS: Virgin Islands' finances called 'precarious'.
newsitem.headline: Virgin Islands' finances called 'precarious'.

text.p: The U.S. Virgin Islands government will have only $4 million in its general fund by the end of the month and still owes vendors $63 million, Acting Finance Commissioner Juan Centeno said.
"The Virgin Islands government is in the most precarious position it's been in for a long time," Centeno told the island's Senate Finance Committee on Thursday.
Centeno said there was $10 million in the islands' general fund and that only $4 million would be left after the next payroll is met on July 31.
The government has other debts in addition to the $63 million owed to vendors, said Centeno, who hoped to provide a total deficit figure next week.
He said the U.S. territory in the Caribbean had lost 4,000 businesses in the last two years, severely curtailing tax revenues flowing into the treasury.
The islands' economy has been devastated by a series of destructive hurricanes.
